cases.expected: byte[] length <= 512 and Message.size equals returned byte[].length
cases.description: A typical DNS query message (one question record, no answer/authority/additional sections) is converted with a maxLength far larger than the actual wire size. The method should succeed, return the complete wire format, and set the internal size field to the number of bytes written.

Create a message whose wire representation is exactly 128 bytes (e.g., a query with several additional OPT records). Calling toWire(128) must succeed without truncation, returning a byte array whose length equals the supplied maxLength.

When the generated wire size is larger than the supplied maxLength, the private toWire method should truncate the output to the allowed length (the public toWire(int) does not expose a truncate flag, so the implementation must honour the limit). The returned array must be exactly maxLength bytes long and the size field must reflect the truncated length.

If the implementation decides that truncation would produce an invalid DNS message (e.g., the header itself cannot fit), it should throw MessageSizeExceededException. Supplying a maxLength smaller than the minimum DNS header (12 bytes) validates this error path.
The method must validate its argument. Passing a negative maxLength should result in an IllegalArgumentException before any wire conversion is attempted.

group: Message with TSIG – signed message handling

cases.expected: byte[] length <= 1024, includes TSIG record at the end, and Message.size matches byte[].length
cases.description: Create a message, add a TSIG record (using setTSIG) and verify that toWire correctly appends the TSIG MAC and updates the size field. The output must still respect the maxLength limit.
A freshly created Message contains only the DNS header (12 bytes). Calling toWire(12) should succeed, return exactly 12 bytes and set the internal size field to 12.
The method must reject a maxLength of zero because a DNS message cannot be empty. An IllegalArgumentException should be thrown before any wire conversion takes place.

cases.expected: byte[] length <= 65535 and Message.size equals returned byte[].length
cases.description: Create a Message that fills the DNS UDP payload limit (e.g., many records across all sections). Calling toWire(Message.MAXLENGTH) must succeed, returning a byte array whose length does not exceed 65535 and updating the size field accordingly.

group: Complex message – multiple sections without truncation

cases.expected: byte[] length <= 1024 and Message.size equals returned byte[].length; all added records are present in the wire output
cases.description: Add records to the answer, authority, and additional sections (including an OPT pseudo‑record). The total wire size is well under 1024 bytes. toWire(1024) should serialize the full message, preserve the order of sections, and set size to the exact byte count.

group: Repeated toWire calls – size field consistency

cases.expected: first call: size == first byte[].length; second call with larger maxLength: size == second byte[].length (updated); both arrays contain correct wire data
cases.description: Invoke toWire(512) on a Message, then add an extra record and invoke toWire(1024). Verify that the internal size field reflects the most recent conversion and that each returned byte array is correct for its respective call.

group: TSIG present but maxLength too small – exception path

cases.description: Create a signed Message with a TSIG record (approximately 20‑30 bytes). A maxLength that can hold the header and question but not the full TSIG should cause the method to abort with MessageSizeExceededException rather than produce a truncated, invalid TSIG.

group: Very large maxLength – larger than any possible wire size

cases.expected: byte[] length == actual wire size (<= Message.MAXLENGTH) and Message.size equals that length
cases.description: Pass a maxLength far exceeding the protocol limit (e.g., 200 000). The implementation should ignore the oversized limit, serialize the message up to its natural size (≤ 65535), and set size accordingly without throwing.

group: Header only with insufficient maxLength for question

cases.description: Create a Message that contains a question record (the minimal non‑header DNS message). Calling toWire(12) provides space only for the DNS header, so the method must abort and throw MessageSizeExceededException because the question cannot be encoded.

The DNS protocol caps a UDP message at 65535 bytes (Message.MAXLENGTH). Supplying a maxLength larger than this constant should be rejected with IllegalArgumentException before any serialization occurs.
